questions.q: What namespace do every one of Purview's built-in system classifications' formal names fall under?
options: The reserved MICROSOFT. namespace
A namespace the user chooses at scan time
They have no formal names, only display names
The CUSTOM. namespace
questions.explain: Every system classification's formal name is grouped under the reserved MICROSOFT. namespace — for example, MICROSOFT.GOVERNMENT.US.SOCIAL_SECURITY_NUMBER.

questions.q: What permission do you need to create a custom classification?
options: Global Administrator on the Azure tenant
Data Curator or Data Source Administrator permission on any collection
No permission is required — anyone can create one
Policy Author at the root collection only
questions.explain: Creating a custom classification requires Data Curator or Data Source Administrator permission on any collection — permission at any collection level is sufficient.

questions.q: If you name a custom classification 'contoso.hr.employee_ID', what friendly name does the portal generate?
options: Contoso.Hr.Employee ID
EMPLOYEE_ID
Hr.Employee ID
contoso.hr.employee_ID (unchanged)
questions.explain: The portal trims all but the last two namespace segments, capitalizes the first letter of each word, and replaces underscores with spaces — turning contoso.hr.employee_ID into the friendly name Hr.Employee ID.

questions.q: After creating a custom classification, what is still needed before a scan will automatically apply it to matching data?
options: Nothing else — the classification alone is sufficient
A classification rule (regex or dictionary) that tells the scanner what pattern to match
A new Purview account
A sensitivity label must be created first
questions.explain: A classification by itself is just a label. A classification rule — built as a regular expression or a dictionary — is what actually tells the scanner what data pattern to look for and match automatically.

questions.q: Custom classification rules apply to which kinds of data sources and file types?
options: Only unstructured file types, like DOC and PDF
Every file type without exception
Only image files
Structured sources and file types — like SQL, CosmosDB, CSV, JSON, and Parquet
questions.explain: Custom classifications only apply to structured data sources (like SQL and CosmosDB) and structured file types (CSV, JSON, Parquet) — they are not applied to unstructured file types such as DOC, PDF, or XLSX.
